    String modules as block quivers #

    For a string w and a block space V, the block quiver of w has positions 0, …, n, the moves of the string diagram and identity isomorphisms; for V = k it is the string module, in general it is M(w) ⊗ V.

    Along a string the signs alternate (st_ne_en), so each position has at most one traversal of each sign. At position p the half-word in the direction of sign s (half p s) is the maximal walk; hence the pair functors of M(w) ⊗ V are counted by the positions of w.

      theorem BrickAccessibility.Word.trav_iff {k : Type u} [Field k] {B : Type u} [Ring B] [Algebra k B] {D : MonomialData k B} (w : Word D.Q) {V : Type u} [AddCommGroup V] [Module k V] (hs : IsString D w) (p q : Fin (w.len + 1)) (l : Letter D.Q) :
